html:
The Irish War of Independence was a guerrilla war fought from 1919 to 1921 by the Irish Republican Army against British forces in Ireland.

It began on the day the newly elected Sinn Féin MPs met in Dublin as the Dáil and declared independence. Led by Michael Collins, the IRA ambushed police and soldiers, while the Dáil set up its own courts and taxes. Britain sent in irregular forces, the Black and Tans and the Auxiliaries, whose reprisals, such as the burning of Cork, turned opinion against it.

About 2,000 people died. A truce came in July 1921 and talks led to the Anglo-Irish Treaty. The war grew out of the Easter Rising, and the IRA drew members from the GAA. See Ireland.
sum: The Irish War of Independence was a guerrilla war fought from 1919 to 1921 by the Irish Republican Army against British forces in Ireland.
